_meta.note: Regression reference for Justify My Meeting (renamed from Meeting BS Detector, 2026-09-02 — the v1 goldens were discarded because they exercised eleven endpoints that no longer exist). Re-run with `npm run check:golden justify-my-meeting` against a local backend and diff for QUALITY, not exact match. Beyond what check-golden asserts automatically, eyeball these by hand, because no gate sees them: (1) every number in every prose field must trace to something the visitor supplied — the arithmetic lives in timeFootprint()/totals and nowhere else; (2) `verdict`, `better_format.recommendation` and `per_meeting[].read` must be EXACTLY the English enum strings, since the frontend looks them up to pick a colour and a t() key; (3) nothing may tell the visitor they are allowed to skip, and no message may announce rather than propose. Each case carries its own `guards` line saying what it is there to catch. See audit/tool-notes/JUSTIFYMYMEETING-NOTES.md.

cases.name: judge-with-numbers
cases.guards: person_hours must equal duration x attendees (22), computed in code. Also the three overreaches the 2026-09-03 grounding pass removed, all of which the model produced here before: it must NOT generalise the visitor's own 90 seconds to the rest of the room, must NOT read six months of recurrence as habit or lack of redesign, and must NOT read no-prep as low engagement. what_earns_the_meeting must be established or explicitly conditional — never invented to balance the verdict — and must not call the discussion contested.

input.meetingText: Weekly engineering all-hands. Standing 60-minute meeting, 22 attendees. Agenda: status updates from each team lead. No prep, no decisions, everyone reports out what they did last week. Recurring for six months.
input.context: I am one of the team leads. I speak for about 90 seconds and listen for the rest.

output.one_liner: Sixty minutes of synchronized listening is not a meeting — it is a newsletter with attendance required.
what_we_know: Agenda consists of status updates from each team lead
No preparation is required of attendees
No decisions are described as part of the format
The visitor is a team lead who speaks for about 90 seconds and listens for the remainder
why_this_verdict: The described purpose is information delivery — each team lead reports what happened last week — and the input does not establish that real-time interaction is part of how that value is created
No decisions, no described discussion, no stated coordination dependency: the input does not establish any function that requires these people to be present simultaneously
The visitor's own airtime establishes only what they do; the input does not establish how the other 21 attendees use their time or whether they are doing anything other than listening
The meeting has recurred for six months, which makes it worth asking whether the format has been deliberately maintained or simply inherited — the input does not establish which
what_earns_the_meeting: If questions or escalations arise during reports, live discussion can catch cross-team dependencies that would otherwise land in separate threads — but the input does not establish whether this happens
what_weakens_the_case: Status updates that do not require immediate response or cross-team negotiation can be read on each person's own time without synchronizing 22 schedules
No prep requirement means attendees arrive without context they could have used to ask better questions, which reduces the upside of being live
The visitor's description — report out what was done last week — frames the meeting as backward-looking delivery, not forward-looking coordination
unknowns_that_matter: Whether live questions, escalations, or cross-team coordination actually occur during or after the reports
Whether leadership uses the meeting to set direction, share context, or make announcements that benefit from being heard together
Whether an async channel already exists and has failed, which would be relevant to whether async is actually a viable replacement here

better_format.how: Replace the standing meeting with a shared written update — each team lead posts their status before a set deadline — and hold a short live session only in weeks where something requires real-time discussion or decision.
better_format.assumptions: Team leads can reliably post updates on schedule, and there is a channel where people will actually read them.

output.next_move: Bring a specific proposal to whoever owns the meeting: pilot a four-week async format, track whether anything gets missed, and use the result to decide whether the live slot earns its place.
if_it_has_to_happen: Flip the format: post written updates in advance and use the live time only for questions, blockers, and cross-team coordination that genuinely needs the room
Cap each report to what others actually need to act on — not a summary of last week but a flag of what affects them this week
Build in an explicit standing item for decisions or escalations so the meeting has at least one moment that only works live

cases.name: judge-no-numbers
cases.guards: No duration, no headcount. time_footprint must come back all-null, and no field may state a figure ABOUT THE MEETING that the visitor did not supply. Numbers inside a PROPOSAL are fine: 'circulate the deck 24 hours ahead' invents nothing about this meeting. The line is claim versus suggestion, not the presence of a digit.

input.meetingText: Recurring 'project sync' with no agenda in the invite. In practice the organiser talks through a slide deck and asks at the end whether anyone has questions. Usually nobody does.

output.one_liner: This is a slide presentation with an audience, not a meeting — and the silence at the end proves nobody is there to disagree.
what_we_know: The meeting recurs under the label 'project sync'
No agenda is included in the invite
In practice, the organiser presents a slide deck
Questions are invited at the end
why_this_verdict: The described format — organiser presents, attendees receive, silence follows — is one-directional, which makes the synchronous time hard to justify on its own terms

The absence of questions at the end is observable, but what it establishes is limited: it could mean the content is clear, that people are disengaged, that questions arise later, or that the format discourages them — the input does not establish which
The meeting recurs, which makes it worth asking whether the format has been deliberately designed or simply repeated — but recurrence alone does not answer that question
No agenda in the invite is established; whether that reflects the meeting's actual structure or just the invite is not established
what_earns_the_meeting: A recurring sync can create a shared rhythm and a predictable moment for the team to surface issues — the input does not establish whether this happens here, but it is possible
what_weakens_the_case: One-way information delivery does not require everyone present at the same time
Consistent silence after the question prompt suggests the format may not be creating space for real discussion
No agenda means attendees arrive without knowing what they are there to contribute
unknowns_that_matter: Whether attendees use the meeting to coordinate with each other, not just receive from the organiser
Whether decisions, blockers, or cross-team dependencies surface during or around this meeting
How many people attend and how long it runs — both would clarify the cost of the current format

better_format.how: Send the slide deck ahead of the meeting with a short written summary; reserve the live time only for questions, decisions, or coordination that genuinely require the group together.
better_format.assumptions: Attendees would read the materials before the meeting — if that is unlikely, a shorter live walkthrough followed by structured discussion may work better than async-first.

output.next_move: Ask the organiser — or yourself if you are the organiser — what would be lost if the deck were sent by email instead, and what the live time would then be used for.
if_it_has_to_happen: Add an agenda to the invite so attendees know what they are expected to contribute, not just receive
Replace the open 'any questions?' with two or three specific prompts: what is blocked, what is at risk, what needs a decision this week
Consider ending the meeting early if the structured discussion takes less time than the slot — the silence is a signal, not a problem to fill

cases.name: zombie
cases.guards: Weekly + duration + attendees, so occurrences_per_year (52) and annual_person_hours (156) are computed from PER_YEAR in code. what_would_be_lost must hold established value or explicitly conditional possibilities only — no invented 'informal coordination', 'soft accountability' or team cohesion, and nothing inferred from people joining from their cars.

input.originalPurpose: Set up when we were launching the new site — we needed everyone in one place daily while things were breaking.
input.whatActuallyHappens: The site launched fourteen months ago. Now it is six people reading their Asana tasks aloud. Two people join from their cars.

output.one_liner: The crisis that created this meeting ended fourteen months ago; what remains is six people reading a task manager aloud.
output.then_and_now: It was built for a live site launch where daily real-time coordination was the point. The launch is long over, and what happens now is task recitation from Asana — something Asana already does without a meeting.
what_would_be_lost: Nothing specific was established from what you told me. That does not mean the meeting provides no value; it means any value beyond what you described is unknown.

what_to_change.why: The original purpose is gone and the current format — reading tasks aloud — provides nothing that requires six people to be live at the same time

what_to_change.change: If any coordination is still needed, replace with an async Asana update plus a standing rule: flag anything that needs a live decision and call a focused conversation only then
what_to_change.why: Synchronous time would be spent on something that actually requires it rather than on information Asana already holds

unknowns_that_matter: Whether anything other than task recitation happens — side conversation, unblocking, decisions — that was not described
Whether the two people joining from cars are doing so because the meeting does not warrant stopping, or simply because of scheduling
output.next_move: Name the meeting as the zombie it appears to be in your next team conversation, ask if anyone can name something the live format accomplishes that Asana cannot, and if no one can, cancel it.

cases.name: zombie-no-original-purpose
cases.guards: then_and_now must SAY the original purpose was not supplied rather than inventing one, and the absence must not itself be treated as evidence the meeting is dead.

input.whatActuallyHappens: Someone shares a dashboard and asks if anyone has questions. It ends 20 minutes early most weeks.

output.one_liner: A dashboard someone could email is holding 11 people hostage for 40 minutes every two weeks.
output.then_and_now: The original purpose was not supplied. What happens now is one person shares a dashboard and asks for questions — a format that ends 20 minutes early most weeks.
what_synchronous_still_does: Questions about the dashboard can be asked live, if anyone has them
what_would_be_lost: Nothing specific was established from what you told me. That does not mean the meeting provides no value; it means any value beyond what you described is unknown.

what_to_change.change: Replace the meeting with a shared dashboard link and an async comment thread
what_to_change.why: If the live format consistently ends early and the main act is a shared screen, the synchronous time is not doing work that async cannot

what_to_change.change: If any live meeting is kept, cut the slot to 20 minutes to match actual usage
what_to_change.why: The meeting already runs 20 minutes most weeks — the 60-minute block is fiction

unknowns_that_matter: Whether questions raised during the meeting lead to decisions or actions that depend on real-time discussion
Whether any coordination, escalation or cross-team alignment actually happens in the room
Whether the dashboard is accessible to all 11 attendees between meetings
output.next_move: Ask the group in the next session whether anyone needs the live format, or whether a shared link with a comment thread would meet the same need.

cases.name: week
cases.guards: One per_meeting entry per supplied meeting. `read` pinned to exact English AND `name` pinned in code to the supplied meeting name — one run copied the whole rendered list line into `name`, which the frontend prints as the card heading. The 1:1 has no purpose supplied, so it MUST be 'not enough to tell': supplying the conventional purpose of a 1:1 and grading against it is the failure this case exists to catch. totals computed in code: 3.5h, 37 person-hours (0.5x8 + 1x5 + 2x14), 1 meeting missing numbers. summary must contain no counts, totals or ranges.

meetings.name: Monday standup
meetings.purpose: What everyone is working on this week

meetings.name: Design review
meetings.purpose: Decide whether the checkout flow ships

output.summary: A mix of team coordination, a live design decision, a large planning session, and a company-wide recurring meeting — ranging from tightly scoped to open-ended in purpose and scale.

per_meeting.name: Monday standup
per_meeting.why: Sharing what everyone is working on this week is information distribution, and whether that warrants eight people synchronously depends on whether the live exchange produces coordination or questioning that async cannot — that is not established here.

per_meeting.name: Design review
per_meeting.why: A binary ship/no-ship decision on a specific flow is concrete enough to justify a live meeting where questions can surface and the call can be made in the room.

per_meeting.name: Quarterly planning kickoff
per_meeting.why: Setting Q4 priorities is the kind of high-stakes, cross-functional alignment where live discussion catches conflicts and builds shared commitment that a document cannot replicate.

per_meeting.name: All-hands
per_meeting.why: No duration, attendee count, or purpose was supplied, so there is nothing to evaluate.

opportunities.change: Replace with a shared async update and use the slot only for exceptions
opportunities.what_it_assumes: Attendees can actually surface blockers or coordination needs in writing before the week gets moving

opportunities.change: Narrow attendance to decision-makers and one subject-matter voice per dependency
opportunities.what_it_assumes: Fourteen attendees includes some who are there to receive the outcome rather than shape it

opportunities.change: Confirm whether the full hour is needed or whether the ship decision can close the meeting early
opportunities.what_it_assumes: The decision is not consistently contested in ways that require the full slot

output.shape_of_the_week: No timing data was supplied for any meeting, so concentration or fragmentation across the day cannot be assessed.
unknowns_that_matter: All-hands: duration, headcount, and purpose — without these it cannot be evaluated at all
Monday standup: whether the eight attendees actually coordinate work in real time or mostly listen
Quarterly planning kickoff: how many of the fourteen attendees are expected to contribute versus receive the outcome
output.next_move: Get the All-hands details and then decide whether the Monday standup is doing coordination work or just delivering information that could travel async.

cases.name: rescue
cases.guards: Role is 'Attending', so nothing may assume authority to end, leave or restructure the meeting. softer_version must not assume a separate conversation will be scheduled or that anyone wants one — it offers it as a question the room answers. after_the_meeting must be something THEY do.

input.whatsHappening: We are 35 minutes into a 45-minute meeting and we have not reached the thing it was called for. Two people are relitigating a decision that was made last month.

output.the_problem: With 10 minutes left, the meeting's stated purpose has not been reached because two attendees are reopening a decision that was already made.
output.say_this_now: Can we park the previous decision for now — we have 10 minutes left and we have not gotten to the thing this meeting was called for. What do we need to decide before we lose the room?
output.softer_version: I want to make sure we get to the original agenda item before we run out of time — would it help to note the concern about last month's decision separately and come back to it, so we can use these last few minutes for what we scheduled today?
output.if_youre_not_running_it: Ask a question rather than redirect: 'Are we going to get to the main agenda item today, or should we figure out how to reschedule it?' — that puts the choice to the room without you having to chair it.
output.if_its_time_to_wrap: Name what is unresolved and ask who owns the next step: 'It looks like we did not reach the agenda item — can someone confirm whether we are scheduling a follow-up or handling it another way?'
output.after_the_meeting: Send a short note to whoever called the meeting noting that the agenda item was not reached and asking how they want to handle it — so the ball is visibly in someone else's court.

cases.name: agenda-after-fix-it
cases.guards: The follow-up a FIX IT verdict earns, and the case that catches the agenda arguing against the old meeting instead of designing the new one. NO field may criticise the existing format, invent blockers, dependencies, decisions or coordination needs, or describe what attendees already know or could have read. Items that depend on something unestablished must be conditional. live_agenda minutes may total well under the duration — padding to fill the slot right after recommending a shorter meeting is the contradiction this guards.

input.meetingText: Weekly engineering all-hands. Standing 60-minute meeting, 22 attendees. Agenda: status updates from each team lead. No prep, no decisions, everyone reports out what they did last week. Recurring for six months.
input.context: I am one of the team leads. I speak for about 90 seconds and listen for the rest.

output.why_are_we_meeting: Live time is for surfacing issues, dependencies, or decisions that require the group to be in the room together — things that emerged from last week and cannot wait or be resolved by one person alone. Status that needs no response from the group moves out of the room.
what_must_be_true_when_we_leave: Any cross-team blocker or dependency that needs group awareness has been named and owns a next step
Any decision that requires input from multiple teams has been made or assigned an owner and deadline
Anyone who needs help from another team has asked for it and received a response
who_needs_to_participate: Someone who can speak to what their team is working on and flag anything that needs another team
Someone with authority to assign ownership or unblock a cross-team issue if one arises
Anyone whose work is currently blocked by or blocking another team present
before_the_meeting: Each team lead posts a written status update — what shipped, what is in progress, what is stuck — in a shared doc or channel before the meeting
Any team lead who has nothing to raise beyond their written update marks themselves as 'no live item' so the room knows whose time is actually needed

live_agenda.item: Any team lead who flagged a live item presents it — one or two sentences on the situation and what they need from the group
live_agenda.why_live: The group can ask questions, offer context, surface dependencies, and agree on a path in real time rather than over a thread

live_agenda.item: Group responds: who owns the resolution, what is the next step, by when
live_agenda.why_live: Commitment made in front of the group carries accountability that an async reply does not

output.end_with: Close by naming every open item, its owner, and its deadline — if no live items were flagged that week, the meeting does not need to happen and the written updates stand on their own.

cases.name: message-after-make-it-async
cases.guards: The follow-up a MAKE IT ASYNC verdict earns. The message must PROPOSE, never announce, and must never state that the visitor will skip.

input.meetingText: Weekly engineering all-hands. Standing 60-minute meeting, 22 attendees. Agenda: status updates from each team lead. No prep, no decisions, everyone reports out what they did last week. Recurring for six months.
input.better: Written updates from each lead before a deadline, plus a 20-minute sync kept only for what needs live discussion.

output.message: I wanted to run an idea by you about the weekly all-hands. What if each lead submitted a written update by, say, end of day Monday, and we kept a 20-minute slot for anything that actually needs live discussion? My hunch is we'd get the same awareness with less time ask on everyone — but you know the group better than I do, so I'd want your read on it.
output.why_it_lands: It frames the change as a question, credits the manager's judgment, and names a concrete structure rather than just complaining about the current one.
output.if_they_say_no: Good to know — happy to stick with the current format. If it ever feels like the right moment to revisit, I'm glad to put together a quick proposal.
output.do_not_send: Any version that opens with 'these meetings feel like a waste of time' — it puts the manager on the defensive before the idea gets a fair hearing.
